**File permissions won't protect your SSH keys. Neither will a password vault.**

Serge Gatezh moved his keys into his Mac's Secure Enclave.

**Now every SSH connection waits for his fingerprint.**

Three plans, per his write-up.

**Which did you try first? Save this.**
bullets: Key file in ~/.ssh: any script that reads your disk can copy it.
Password vault: the key still gets decrypted in memory to sign.
Works: a key made in hardware that never leaves it, Touch ID on every use.
